verdicts.claim: Full effects (Reduce flashing off) fail the flash check on main (normal signature 3.5 primary, 5 area-15%), so public builds lock Reduce flashing on and hide the toggle; a normal-mode FAIL blocks any toggle restore or release.
verdicts.what_is_true: Full effects read over 3 on the project's own analyser in committed records: the signature reads 3.5/5/3 on main of 2026-10-27 (Tools' bisect doc, no saved output), and normal seed clips read 3.5 on the pin (nightly-seeds.json). The live /play/ pack has lock_reduce_flashing true and Reduce flashing on by default, and the LAN kit locks it too, so nobody can reach full effects. Today's main has no normal-mode reading. Legal's 'blocks any release' also clashes with its own addendum 10 option (b), a release with only the calm look.
proof: audit/2026-11-07/evidence/AC-001.txt (live pack: "lock_reduce_flashing": true, reduce_flashing default true)
audit/2026-11-07/evidence/AC-003.txt (nightly-seeds.json: ai-1029-normal and ai-1049-normal at 3.5 on 257a766c)
external: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/three-flashes-or-below-threshold.html (accessed 2026-11-07), SC 2.3.1 Level A: "anything that flashes more than three times in any one second period"
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Low. The lock is the right control, but reading 'blocks any release' as absolute would rule out the release with only the calm look that Legal itself allows.
verdicts.fix: Keep the lock. Measure today's main in normal mode and save the output before restoring the toggle. Reword the rule to 'blocks offering full effects'.

verdicts.claim: The project's own analyser finds scenes in the public build over 3 flashes a second (building fly-past 4.5, beam impacts 4.5 and 3.5) that Reduced mode does not fix; they are not fixed and flash work has been paused since 2026-10-18.
verdicts.what_is_true: In the mode players get, the live pin 257a766c has a seed clip at 3.5 (ai-1047-reduced, 2026-10-28, in tools/web-template.json), and the signature clip reads 3/3/3. So the project's own analyser, which has never been checked against a recognised one, does find a public scene over WCAG's limit of 3. The 4.5, 4.5 and 3.5 figures come from 2026-10-06 builds, and the fly-past (collapse) clip now reads 2 in both modes. 'Paused' is the EP's reading: Orb's own words of 2026-10-18 also say 'keep working on it until it gets solved'.
proof: tools/web-template.json measured.nightly (max 3.5, ai-1047-reduced) and measured.collapse (primary 2 both modes)
external: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/three-flashes-or-below-threshold.html (accessed 2026-11-07): "anything that flashes more than three times in any one second period"
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: The stale 4.5 figures, which README and the review list still carry, make the live build look worse than it reads and steer fixes to the fly-past, which now reads 2.
verdicts.fix: Correct the record with the pin's current readings in each mode. Run a fresh nightly (none since 2026-10-30) and save the output. Fix the flashing scenes, and get an independent analyser's reading before any store release.

verdicts.claim: Orb's owner interim keeps the playable demo public with scenes over 3 a second behind a click-through, no autoplay, Reduce flashing locked on, noindex, no promotion, a pinned measured commit and a kill switch; it comes down on any new scene over 3.5, any report or an unmeasured build swap; Legal records it as ORB'S DECISION, NOT A LEGAL PASS.
verdicts.what_is_true: The waiver is real and in force. /play/ serves pin 257a766c behind a gate with a start button, carries noindex, and has Reduce flashing locked on in the live pack. The interim runs to 2026-11-15, and RL-161 says 'ORB'S DECISION, NOT A LEGAL PASS'. Two safeguards do not work. No nightly has run since 2026-10-30, and the 2026-10-28 run already had a reduced clip at the 3.5 line. The one-command kill switch publishes only through ci.yml's deploy job, which has run nothing for 37 pushes. The expiry and RL-207's 2026-11-08 string deadline only fail a CI check, so nothing takes the demo down on those dates.
proof: tools/site-offline.mjs:4 ("Commit and push the file to publish it")
external: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/three-flashes-or-below-threshold.html (accessed 2026-11-07): "anything that flashes more than three times in any one second period"
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: None from the record itself. The danger is in trusting that the kill switch, the nightly and the expiry still work.
verdicts.fix: Quote the four step names at ci.yml:226, 240, 263 and 277 so deploys and the kill switch work again, or have Orb unpublish Pages by hand. Restart the nightly and add an alarm when it goes stale. Add a scheduled site check so the expiry date actually does something.

verdicts.claim: Flash rule k05 caps full flashes at 3 a second over the whole screen; before the first public web release there must be a shared flash registry, an automated WCAG 2.3.1 check on worst-case recordings, a reduced-flash setting, a first-start and store notice, and documented results.
verdicts.what_is_true: k05 and the web conditions state WCAG 2.3.1 correctly: 3 flashes a second, 25% of a 10-degree field, a 341x256 window at 1024x768. Their parts all exist at the live pin: the shared register, the project's own analyser (run by hand, not in CI), the locked setting, the click-through notice and the committed records. What is missing is a passing result, which is AC-005's gate. The register cannot see camera or scenery sweeps (flash_registry.gd:24-25), and 'Stage 1b' is never defined.
external: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/three-flashes-or-below-threshold.html (accessed 2026-11-07): 'flashes occurring concurrently occupies no more than a total of .006 steradians' (25% of a 10 degree field)
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Low, since the rule matches the standard. There is a small drift: k05 says reduced mode 'halves the rate', but the register allows 1.0 of a 2.5 budget and CI counts 1 flash per 60 ticks.
verdicts.fix: Record k05 as met in parts at the pin and point its open item at AC-005. Define 'Stage 1b' or drop it. Bring k05's reduced-mode wording in line with the register.

verdicts.claim: Release flash pass: worst second at most 2.5 primary in both modes on the published commit, no sensitivity run above 3, second captures for 2.0-3.0, 20 seeds with the five worst carried, the set re-run on camera, lighting, scenery, effects or crowd changes; per-change subsets and starved captures never count.
verdicts.what_is_true: The rule is written as Legal's margin over WCAG: a clip at exactly 3 'passes the standard but not our gate'. It is coded in tools/flash/verdict.js and release-pass.mjs, which check PASS rows, read the mode back from the game, run a canary pair and compare content hashes. It is not met: the live pin's reduced signature reads 3/3/3 and a reduced seed 3.5, and the owner-interim path skips the recorded pass. ITU-R BT.1702 exists, but the record admits its method was not re-read. The 20-seed and starved-capture rules depend on hand runs I did not check.
external: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/three-flashes-or-below-threshold.html (accessed 2026-11-07): "anything that flashes more than three times in any one second period"

https://www.itu.int/rec/R-REC-BT.1702/en (accessed 2026-11-07): title "Guidance for the reduction of photosensitive epileptic seizures caused by television", BT.1702-3 (11/2023); its transition method not checked
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: None while the 2.5 stays labelled a margin. steam-readiness.md:39 correctly calls it the project's own release gate, not a Steam rule.
verdicts.fix: Keep the rule. Save the pass output for each commit. Once CI works again, run the set whenever the pin moves.

verdicts.claim: The flash check must run as a CI gate on the full required set, so that a camera, VFX or scenery change cannot reintroduce a failure.
verdicts.what_is_true: No full-set pixel gate exists. ci.yml:103-104 says the CI flash job only counts register requests and the pixel half 'is not in CI yet', and CI has run no job since 3c9005ac. Under the owner interim a pin move needs only the signature record (check-site-interim.mjs:442-447), not a recorded pass (site-pin.mjs:29-32), and the pin did move once without a measurement (86d44e54). The full-set path does refuse content whose hash differs from the recorded pass, so the gap belongs to the owner interim.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Running the full 76-clip pixel set in CI would mean hours of headless capture on every push. A narrower gate, a fresh pixel record for the exact pin before deploy, closes the same gap.
verdicts.fix: Make check-site-interim.mjs require a pixel record for the exact pin before the pin moves. Run the full set on a schedule, not on every push.

verdicts.claim: The public flash notice must be true on the day and use Legal's fixed words identically on the gate, the page box and in game; never 'safe', 'seizure-safe', 'tested', 'compliant', 'certified' or 'no flashing'; 'we are fixing them' has been untrue since flash work paused.
verdicts.what_is_true: The /play/ gate and the holding page carry Legal's fixed words, and none of the banned words appears on them or in README. But the public README still says the hosted build 'is offline for now' and 'We are fixing them'. The live game pack still holds 'We are fixing them.' and the old menu notice, which tools/site-ui-excuse.json excuses until 2026-11-08. RL-207 says the demo then goes to the holding page, but a failing check takes nothing down, and CI is not running at all.
proof: audit/2026-11-07/evidence/AC-007.txt (live pack and 257a766c terms.json vs HEAD)
docs/accessibility/audit-2026-10-28.md:100 (says the words are met, true only for HEAD data)
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Low. The stale words either understate that the build is up or promise a fix, but every version still tells photosensitive players not to play.
verdicts.fix: Replace README lines 7 and 9 with the words from page-fixed-lines.md. By 2026-11-08, either move the pin (after a nightly) or take the demo down, as RL-207 says. Either one needs CI repaired or Pages unpublished by hand.

verdicts.claim: After the 2026-10-17 take-down a second interim is allowed only if the whole set reads at most 3 primary in both modes with the hook corrected, 20 more seeds are clean, the toggle is hidden unless full effects pass, and the hook is proven with read-back and a canary clip.
verdicts.what_is_true: RL-156 and addendum 10 set out this gate exactly as quoted. It was never met: addendum 11 and RL-161 put the demo back up as Orb's decision instead, so the gate was superseded, not passed. Its lasting parts are in force: the toggle is locked in the live pack, and release-pass.mjs requires the Reduce flashing state read back from the game and a canary pair.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: An open row for a gate that can no longer be passed adds to the open count and blurs which interim rules apply.
verdicts.fix: Retire RL-156's return gate as superseded by RL-161. Keep its read-back and canary rules under the release pass (AC-005).

verdicts.claim: The camera cut's whole-screen dip and the building fly-past count as full-screen flashes and must be capped or fixed before public release, whatever the Reduce flashing default; the README names the camera fly-past of collapsing buildings as over the limit.
verdicts.what_is_true: Under WCAG, a whole-screen luminance change does count across the whole area. But at the live pin the cut's dip is CUT_DIM 0.09, under the 0.10 flash step, and pane cuts are held to one a second. The collapse (fly-past) clip on the pin reads 2 on the primary reading in both modes; its 3.5 is the stricter area reading in full effects, which are locked away. So README's naming of the fly-past is stale. Addendum 10's 'prefer a dissolve' clashes with Orb's 2026-10-18 ban on dissolves, though it was marked as advice, not a ruling.
external: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/three-flashes-or-below-threshold.html (accessed 2026-11-07): "anything that flashes more than three times in any one second period"
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: It keeps RL-117 open 'until Camera fixes', shows the public a stale finding in README, and could push Camera toward the dissolves Orb banned.
verdicts.fix: Correct the record. Close the dip item against CUT_DIM 0.09 at the pin and update README to the page-fixed-lines.md words. Keep the cut and collapse clips in the release set, and drop the dissolve advice.

verdicts.claim: The camera swing must pass the flash clips before any public pin. A full 360-degree swing reads 3.5 at 960x540, which fails the release gate.
verdicts.what_is_true: The 3.5 figure is a table in docs/world/ring-any-angle/rendering.md:359, measured in a scratch copy of the game, with no saved output. DirSwing is switched off ("enabled": false) at HEAD and at a8bc66e2, and the pin predates the swing data, so no build anyone plays carries it; 'private build only' overstates its reach. The rule itself is sound but already covered by AC-005's re-run-on-camera-change rule. I did not check other swing paths in the LAN build.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Small: an open row, plus a reading that could lead to a swing-rate cap before the real feature has been measured.
verdicts.fix: Retire the separate row. When DirSwing is turned on, run the swing clips under the release rule and save the output.

verdicts.claim: The pin moved on 2026-10-19 with no nightly run (a take-down trigger); after the 2026-10-22 take-down, restore on 257a766c needs a nightly with none over 3.5 primary, true 'not fixed yet' gate words and the gap recorded, without restarting the clock.
verdicts.what_is_true: 86d44e54 took the site down because the pin moved to 257a766c on 2026-10-19 without a nightly. f00357f7 then recorded the nightly (max 3.5 in normal, 2.5 in reduced), 14c284ff restored the site on 2026-10-22, and the live gate says 'they are not fixed yet'. The episode is closed, but RL-169 and RL-171 still read Open. It is the one recorded case of the gap described in AC-006.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Two stale Open rows inflate the open count.
verdicts.fix: Close RL-169 and RL-171 as met, citing f00357f7 and 14c284ff.

verdicts.claim: Once either PC draws the other fight in 2v2, one flash register per screen sums both fights (3 light events a second, primary 2.5, L* 86), calm beams still count, the other fight gives way, and 2v2 clips run in both modes, day and night, before anyone but Orb sees it; ?otherfights=1 never reaches a public build.
verdicts.what_is_true: RL-249 (review-log.md:271) sets these conditions for drawing the partner's fight, after RL-241 (:263). The LAN folder does not pass --others, so the drawn case is in nobody's build. ?otherfights=1 is read only where bypass_allowed() is true, which is never in a locked build without the capture hook or on a public host, and the word is absent from the live pin and pack. The inventory's notes are wrong: RL-247 has a row (:269), RL-249 sits in the summary table, and :463 is a Sources line. 'Anyone but Orb' now includes Orb 2 (RL-253).
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Low: a private-build gate sitting in the safety log. The wrong notes could send someone looking for an RL-247 row that already exists.
verdicts.fix: Keep it as a private-build condition. Correct the inventory's citations, and read 'Orb' as 'Orb and Orb 2', per RL-253.

batch_notes: The live /play/ pack was fetched with curl GET and grepped (AC-001.txt): lock_reduce_flashing is true and Reduce flashing is on by default, but the in-game notice strings are the old 'We are fixing them' ones.

With CI dead, neither the kill switch (site-offline.mjs publishes only through the deploy job) nor the interim's expiry or RL-207's 2026-11-08 string deadline can act. Pages keeps serving the 2026-11-05 deploy until someone unpublishes it by hand.

No nightly has run since 2026-10-30. The 2026-10-28 run is recorded only in tools/web-template.json, not in nightly-seeds.json, and its worst clip was ai-1047-reduced at 3.5: in the mode players get, and exactly at the take-down line.

Every reading in this slice comes from the project's own analyser, which says it is not a recognised one (wcag.js:3). I re-ran no captures (no Godot or Chrome), so every figure rests on committed records.

The claims inventory's notes for AC-012 are wrong: RL-247 exists at review-log.md:269. The accessibility audit (2026-10-28:100) calls the notice words met, which is true for HEAD data but not for the live pin.
